newsitem.title: USA: NRC fines PSE&G N.J. power plants.
newsitem.headline: NRC fines PSE&G N.J. power plants.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Thursday it levied a $180,000 fine against Public Service Electric & Gas Co (PSE&G), operator of the Salem and Hope Creek nuclear generating facilities in New Jersey.
A PSE&G spokeswoman said, "We won't contest it. We're not challenging the violations," a PSE&G spokeswoman said.
But the company might challenge the size of the fine following actions it has taken to correct the problems at the plants, she said.

The federal agency said the penalty stemmed from three alleged violations of security requirements and one alleged violation involving harassment, intimidation and discrimination against workers at the plants.
PSE&G was also cited, but not fined, for three additional violations dealing with plant security, NRC said.

In a letter to PSE&G, NRC's Region I Administrator Hubert Miller said, "These three violations of fundamental access control requirements at nuclear power plants represent a significant degradation in the security program at the facility,.."

NRC said it wanted to emphasize the significance it attaches to any finding of discrimination, as well as the importance of current management ensuring a safety-conscious environment where employees are not discouraged from voicing safety issue worries, Miller said.

In April 1995, NRC issued a $80,000 penalty to PSE&G for discrimination related to a manager's retaliation against and harrassment of an on-site safety review engineer back in December 1992. The engineer had supported two subordinates who attempted to raise a safety concern.
Public Service Enterprise Group Inc, the parent of PSE&G, and PECO Energy Co each hold a 42.6 percent stake in the two 1,106 megawatt (MW) nuclear units at the Salem facility.
Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Inc each own 7.4 percent interest in Salem.
Both Salem nuclear units, which were shut in 1995, could possibly to resume operation next year.
Public Service Enterprise has 95 percent ownership in the 1,031 MW Hope Creek facility, with Atlantic Energy holding the remaining five percent.
